justification: A tight-aggressive plan for full-ring fixed-limit hold'em, with eight or nine opponents. With so many players still to act, someone often holds a strong hand, so we enter far fewer pots than at six-handed and the first positions are the tightest of all. The under-the-gun range is built to stay sound at both nine and ten seats, since a ten-handed table's two earliest seats both use it. First in, we raise or fold; only the small blind sometimes completes. Behind limpers we raise hands that beat a limping range and call with hands that win big pots when they hit, such as small pairs and suited aces. Facing a single raise we mostly re-raise or fold; callers in between give a better price for speculative hands, and the blinds defend fewer hands against a raiser from under the gun to the lojack than against a later one. Once our own raise is re-raised we call with most of our range and raise again only with the very best hands; when two raises are in and none is ours, we continue only with hands that are strong against one raise, and fewer of them. Overall the chart aims to play roughly 12 to 16 percent of hands voluntarily.

spots.justification: Up to nine players act behind us, so we open only hands that hold up when one of them wakes up: sevens or better, the strong suited aces and suited broadway cards, and ace-queen or better offsuit. Ace-jack offsuit and sixes are edge opens, kept small so the range stays sound at a ten-handed table.
